mainTopic: Partnerships with a גוי or כהן and the gifts of זרוע, לחיים וקבה: marking, partial partnerships, and following the obligation
overview: An animal owned in partnership with a גוי or a כהן is exempt from the gifts of זרוע, לחיים and קבה, but in some cases the Jewish partner must mark the animal so onlookers do not think he is skipping the gifts. The גמרא explains why a גוי partner needs no mark while a כהן partner does: people would not assume a Jew trusts a גוי with his money box, and a גוי partner openly argues about prices, while a modest כהן would not. Next, the גמרא asks why פסולי המוקדשין need no mark, since they are sold like ordinary meat. רב אדא בר אהבה answers that the ruling is about the kind sold only from home. רב הונא and חייא בר רב then argue about a partner in only one part of the animal. רב הונא says this exempts only that part's gift, and חייא בר רב is refuted from ברייתות. רב חסדא explains what misled him: a ברייתא listing the 24 מתנות כהונה counts זרוע, לחיים and קבה as one item, but that is only because they are similar. The גמרא then rules that when a ישראל owns only the head, we follow the part that carries the obligation (בתר חיובא אזלינן). Finally it quotes the משנה's case of a כהן who sells an animal 'except for the gifts.'

steps.title: The gentile is sitting in the butcher shop
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the contradiction by limiting the source that exempts a גוי partnership from marking: it is talking about a גוי who sits in the shop.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with a case where the גוי is sitting in the butcher shop.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction between the sources by saying the 'no marking needed' case is one where the גוי sits right there in the Jew's shop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Marking exists so onlookers know why no gifts are being given. If the גוי sits in the shop, people can see he is a partner, so marking is not needed. The other source, which requires marking, is about a גוי who is not seen in the shop.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what case are we dealing with? (a way of limiting a source to a specific case)
Butcher shop
To mark (put a sign on the animal or meat)
The priestly gifts: זְרוֹעַ, לְחָיַיִם, and קֵיבָה

phrases.english: Here, with what are we dealing?
phrases.notes: "Here" means the source that says a partner of a גוי doesn't need to mark the animal.

phrases.english: Where the gentile sits in the butcher shop.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a contradiction raised just before this section
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sources seemed to argue about whether a גוי partnership needs marking
steps.terutzMaskana: The source that exempts is talking about a גוי visibly sitting in the shop

steps.title: Then the priest also sits in the shop, so why mark?
steps.stepSummary: If the case is a partner sitting in the shop, the same should be true for the כהן case, which requires marking. Why mark there?
steps.simpleTranslation: In the matching case of the כהן, he also sits in the shop. Why does one need to mark?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer: the same source puts the כהן next to the גוי, so the כהן should also be sitting in the shop. Then why does the כהן case require marking?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases are taught side by side, so they should describe the same situation. If sitting in the shop makes the partnership obvious for the גוי, it should do the same for the כהן. So why should the כהן case be any different?

keyTerms.meaning: The matching (parallel) case
Regarding, in the case of
Why?

phrases.english: The corresponding case regarding a priest,
where he sits in the butcher shop,
why must one mark?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the case is a partner sitting in the shop
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cases taught side by side should describe the same setup, so the כהן should not need marking either

steps.title: People will think the priest is buying meat
steps.stepSummary: A כהן sitting in a butcher shop does not look like a partner, because people assume he is a customer buying meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because people will say: he is buying meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a כהן in the shop does not reveal a partnership. Onlookers would just think he came to buy meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What matters is how the scene looks to onlookers. A כהן in a butcher shop looks like an ordinary customer, so the partnership is hidden and marking is still needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat
He is buying
Because people say (think)

phrases.english: Because they say: he is buying meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing how onlookers see the scene
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כהן sitting in the shop would look like a partner
steps.terutzMaskana: Onlookers assume he is a customer, so marking is needed

steps.title: The same could be said of the gentile
steps.stepSummary: If people think a כהן in the shop is buying meat, they would think the same about a גוי. So sitting in the shop proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, about the גוי too people will say: he is buying meat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: a גוי in the shop could also just be a customer, so the first answer does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning from step 3 applies equally to the גוי. That breaks the explanation from step 1, since a גוי sitting in the shop would not show a partnership either.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Also, too

phrases.english: If so, regarding a gentile too they will say:
He is buying meat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of step 3 against the answer of step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the גוי sits in the shop
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a customer explanation hides the כהן's partnership, it hides the גוי's partnership too

steps.title: The gentile sits by the money box
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the first answer and suggests a new one: the גוי sits by the cash box, which shows he is an owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, here we are dealing with a case where the גוי sits by the money box.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer: the source that exempts is talking about a גוי who sits by the cash box where the shop's money goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A customer does not sit by the shop's money. Someone sitting by the cash box looks like an owner, so his partnership is obvious and no marking is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (the earlier answer is dropped)
Money box, safe for the shop's earnings
Sits

phrases.english: Rather, here with what are we dealing?
Where the gentile sits by the money box.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 1
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sitting in the shop shows partnership
steps.terutzMaskana: Sitting by the money box is what shows partnership

steps.title: Then the priest also sits by the money box, so why mark?
steps.stepSummary: Same challenge again: the parallel כהן case should also have him by the money box. Why mark?
steps.simpleTranslation: In the matching case of the כהן, he sits by the money box. Why does one need to mark?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question as in step 2. If the כהן also sits by the cash box, his partnership should be obvious, so why mark?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cases are still parallel. If sitting by the money box reveals the גוי as a partner, it should reveal the כהן too, so the different rule needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Priest, who receives the gifts

phrases.english: The corresponding case regarding a priest, where he sits by the money box,
why must one mark?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same challenge as step 2, now aimed at the answer of step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the partner sits by the money box
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The parallel כהן case should then also be obvious and not need marking

steps.title: People will think the butcher trusts the priest
steps.stepSummary: A כהן by the money box does not look like a partner. People will think the butcher trusts him to guard the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: People will say: he trusts him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that onlookers will think the כהן is a trusted guard of the money, not an owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sitting by the money can have two meanings: owner, or trusted helper. For a כהן, people would assume he is trusted, so the partnership stays hidden and marking is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: He (the butcher) trusts him

phrases.english: They say: he trusts him,
phrases.notes: "He trusts him" means the butcher trusts this person to watch over the money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing how onlookers see the scene
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sitting by the money shows ownership
steps.terutzMaskana: For a כהן, people assume he is simply trusted

steps.title: The same could be said of the gentile
steps.stepSummary: People could also think the butcher simply trusts the גוי, so the money box would not prove partnership for him either.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the גוי too people will say: he trusts him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back again: the 'he is trusted' explanation should apply to a גוי just as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the move of step 4. If trust explains the כהן sitting by the money, it could explain the גוי too, and then the money-box answer falls apart.

phrases.english: Regarding a gentile too they will say: he trusts him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of step 7 against the answer of step 5
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If trust hides the כהן's partnership, it should hide the גוי's partnership too

steps.title: People do not trust a gentile with money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that people would not assume a Jew trusts a גוי with his money, so a גוי by the cash box must be a partner.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no trust in a גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the money-box answer: a Jewish butcher would not normally trust a גוי to guard his money, so onlookers will understand that the גוי is an owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'trusted helper' explanation fits a כהן but not a גוי. So a גוי by the cash box can only be a partner, his partnership is obvious, and no marking is needed. This explains why the two cases get different rules.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no trust

steps.whatToRemember: Marking is only needed when onlookers cannot tell there is a partnership. A גוי by the money box is clearly an owner, but a כהן there could just be a trusted guard.

phrases.english: There is no trust in a gentile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 and holds onto the money-box explanation
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the comparison does not hold
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גוי by the money box might be seen as merely trusted
steps.terutzMaskana: A גוי would not be trusted, so he is seen as a partner

steps.title: A typical gentile partner loudly argues about prices
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: even in the shop itself, a גוי partner shows he is an owner by shouting about prices, while a modest כהן would not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: an ordinary גוי shouts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to explain the difference: a typical גוי partner openly argues and shouts about how things are sold, which reveals that he is an owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here both may simply be sitting in the shop. The גוי's behavior gives away the partnership, but a כהן would quietly let the seller decide, so no one can tell he is a partner, and marking is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say (introduces another answer)
An ordinary, typical
He shouts loudly (about prices and sales)

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers end the discussion: (1) a גוי by the money box must be a partner, since he would not be trusted; (2) a גוי partner shows he is an owner by shouting about prices. Either way, only the כהן's partnership is hidden, so only he needs marking.

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
An ordinary gentile shouts loudly.
phrases.notes: He shouts at the seller about how much to charge, which shows he is an owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא סְתַם גּוֹי מִפְּעָא פָּעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the challenge of step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Another way to tell the cases apart, based on behavior
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גוי and a כהן in the shop look the same
steps.terutzMaskana: The גוי's shouting reveals ownership, but the כהן's quiet manner does not

steps.title: Quoting the ruling that disqualified sacrificial animals need no mark
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא: a butcher selling פסולי המוקדשין does not need to mark them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: And disqualified consecrated animals do not need to be marked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line from the same ברייתא it has been discussing. It is setting up a question on that line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסולי המוקדשין are exempt from the gifts, just like the partnership cases. But here the ברייתא says no sign is needed, unlike a partnership with a כהן, where a sign was required. The next step will ask why.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacrificial animals that became disqualified and were redeemed so they could be eaten as regular meat
To mark, to put up a sign

phrases.english: The Master said: And disqualified consecrated animals
phrases.notes: "The Master" is the תנא of the ברייתא the גמרא has been learning, the same one that said a partner with a כהן must mark but a partner with a גוי need not.

phrases.english: do not need to be marked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the partnership marking cases (Steps 1-10) to a different line in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A butcher selling פסולי המוקדשין is exempt from the gifts and does not need to put up a sign.

steps.title: But disqualified sacrificial animals are sold just like regular meat
steps.stepSummary: No mark is needed only if people can already tell. But a משנה says פסולי המוקדשין are sold, slaughtered and weighed in the market like ordinary meat, so how would anyone know?
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies the matter is obvious. But we learned: disqualified consecrated animals are sold in the meat market, slaughtered in the meat market, and weighed by the litra!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא figures that no mark is needed only because people can already tell the animal is קדשים. It then challenges this with a משנה showing these animals look exactly like regular meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea behind marking is to stop people from thinking a regular animal is exempt. If no mark is needed, the animal's status must be obvious. But the משנה says פסולי המוקדשין are handled in every way like ordinary meat. So nothing shows their status, and they should need a mark too.

keyTerms.meaning: This shows, apparently
The matter is obvious, people can tell on their own
The public meat market
A litra, a unit of weight used for selling meat

phrases.english: This shows that the matter is obvious,
but didn't we learn in a משנה:
Disqualified consecrated animals are sold in the meat market,
and are slaughtered in the meat market,
and are weighed by the litra!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא מוֹכְחָא מִלְּתָא, וְהָא אֲנַן תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from Step 11 and attacks it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in Step 11 that פסולי המוקדשין need no mark.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No mark makes sense only if their status is visible. The משנה shows they are sold just like ordinary meat, so their status is not visible.

steps.title: The ruling is about the kind sold only from home
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה explains that the ברייתא means the type of פסולי המוקדשין that may only be sold from inside the house, so people can tell.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה explained it before רב פפא: it refers to those that are sold inside the house.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה answers the question. The ברייתא is talking about a type of פסולי המוקדשין that is never sold in the market, only from home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some פסולי המוקדשין are sold in the market, and the משנה from Step 12 is about those. Others may only be sold from inside the house. When meat is sold that way, people can tell it is קדשים, so no sign is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it, he interpreted the source
Inside the house, not in the public market

steps.whatToRemember: No sign is needed only when people can tell the meat's status on their own. Selling from home shows it is קדשים.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava explained it
before Rav Pappa,
as referring to those that are sold inside the house.
phrases.notes: These are animals like a בכור or מעשר, which the Sages did not allow to be sold in the open market.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְגְּמָא רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the ברייתא refers to a narrower type of פסולי המוקדשין.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא covers all פסולי המוקדשין, including those sold in the market like regular meat.
steps.terutzMaskana: It refers only to those sold from inside the house, which people can recognize, so no sign is needed.

steps.title: A partner in one part is exempt only from that part's gift
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that if the כהן or גוי is a partner in only one part of the animal, the owner is exempt only from the gift that comes from that part.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: A partner in the head is exempt from the jaw. A partner in the leg is exempt from the foreleg. A partner in the innards is exempt from the maw.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts: partnerships in only part of an animal. רב הונא says the exemption covers only the gift that comes from the shared part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three gifts: the לחי (jaw) comes from the head, the זרוע (foreleg) from the leg, and the קבה (maw) from the innards. רב הונא says each part works on its own. Sharing one part exempts only that part's gift, and the other two must still be given.

keyTerms.meaning: A partner, here a כהן or גוי who owns part of the animal
The jaw, one of the three gifts, taken from the head
The foreleg, one of the three gifts
The maw, the fourth stomach, one of the three gifts

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
A partner in the head is exempt from the jaw,
a partner in the leg is exempt from the foreleg,
phrases.notes: Here יד means the animal's leg and hoof, the part the זרוע gift comes from.

phrases.aramaic: שׁוּתָּף בִּבְנֵי מֵעַיִין – פָּטוּר מִן הַקֵּבָה.
phrases.english: a partner in the innards is exempt from the maw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: partial partnerships, after the marking discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A partnership in one part exempts only the gift that comes from that part.

steps.title: A partner in any one part exempts all the gifts
steps.stepSummary: חייא בר רב disagrees: a partnership in even one part exempts the owner from all three gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חייא בר רב said: Even a partner in one of them is exempt from all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: חייא בר רב argues with רב הונא. He says that sharing even one part of the animal exempts the owner from all three gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא treats each part on its own. חייא בר רב treats the three gifts as one package: once the owner is exempt from one of them, he is exempt from all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt from all of them, all three gifts

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two views straight: רב הונא says exempt only from the matching gift, and חייא בר רב says exempt from all three gifts.

phrases.english: And Chiyya bar Rav said:
Even a partner in just one of them
phrases.notes: "One of them" means one of the three parts: the head, the leg, or the innards.

phrases.english: is exempt from all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב הונא's ruling in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A partnership in any one part exempts the owner from all three gifts.

steps.title: A ברייתא about owning a tiny share of one part
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge חייא בר רב: owning even 1/100 of the head, leg or innards makes the owner exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: "The head is mine and all the rest is yours": even one-hundredth of the head, he is exempt. "The leg is mine and all the rest is yours": even one-hundredth of the leg, he is exempt. "The innards are mine and all the rest is yours": even one-hundredth of them, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא as a challenge to חייא בר רב. It describes partners who own only one part of the animal, or even a tiny share of it, and says the owner is פטור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case in the ברייתא lists only one part of the animal, and the ruling is just "פטור." The challenger seems to read this as meaning exempt from that part's gift only, which fits רב הונא. Step 17 spells out exactly how this attacks חייא בר רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt from the obligation
One part in a hundred, a tiny share

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
"The head is mine and all the rest is yours,"
phrases.notes: Picture a כהן making this deal with an Israelite butcher.

phrases.english: and even if he owns just one-hundredth of the head, he is exempt.
"The leg is mine and all the rest is yours,"
even if he owns just one-hundredth of the leg, he is exempt.
"The innards are mine and all the rest is yours,"
even if he owns just one-hundredth of them, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to test the argument between רב הונא and חייא בר רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: חייא בר רב's view that a partnership in one part exempts all the gifts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא matches each part to its own case and just says "פטור," which seems to mean exempt from that part's gift only. Step 17 spells out the full argument.

steps.title: Reading the ברייתא as exempting only the matching gift
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the ברייתא means that owning part of the head exempts only the jaw, part of the leg exempts only the foreleg, and part of the innards exempts only the maw. That would go against חייא בר רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't it mean: exempt from the jaw but obligated in all the rest; exempt from the foreleg but obligated in all the rest; exempt from the maw but obligated in all the rest?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out how the ברייתא from the last step goes against חייא בר רב. It reads the word 'exempt' as covering only the gift from that body part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא matched each body part with one gift: head, leg, innards. If 'exempt' means only the matching gift, this is exactly רב הונא's view. Then חייא בר רב, who said one part exempts all three gifts, is contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What, is it not...?' The גמרא offers the most natural reading of a source in order to build a challenge
The jaw, one of the three gifts given to the כהן
The foreleg, one of the three gifts
The maw (stomach), one of the three gifts

phrases.english: What, is it not that it means:
exempt from the jaw but obligated in all the rest,
exempt from the foreleg but obligated in all the rest,
exempt from the maw but obligated in all the rest?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the attack hinted at by the ברייתא quoted in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: חייא בר רב's ruling that a partnership in one part exempts from all three gifts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא pairs each body part with its gift. That suggests the exemption covers only the matching gift, not all three.

steps.title: No, it means exempt from all the gifts
steps.stepSummary: The answer on behalf of חייא בר רב: the ברייתא's word 'exempt' means exempt from all the gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means exempt from all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends חייא בר רב. It reads 'exempt' in the ברייתא as a total exemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only said 'exempt' and never said 'obligated in the rest.' So you could read it as fitting חייא בר רב: any partnership in one of these parts frees the owner from all three gifts.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt from all of them, meaning all three gifts

phrases.english: No, he is exempt from all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the reading proposed in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the ambiguous word 'exempt' in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Exempt' means only from the gift of that body part.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Exempt' means from all three gifts, which fits חייא בר רב.

steps.title: Then the ברייתא should have said so
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if the meaning were 'exempt from all,' the ברייתא should have said that clearly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let it teach 'exempt from all of them'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the answer from the last step. A full exemption is a big point, so the ברייתא would have said it outright.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists each part with its own matching gift. If the exemption covered everything, it would have said 'exempt from all' instead of tying each part to one gift. Leaving that out suggests the exemption is limited.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Then let it teach...' meaning the source should have said this clearly if that is what it meant

phrases.english: But then let it teach: exempt from all of them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading of 'exempt' as 'exempt from all.'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא would have said 'exempt from all' clearly if that were its meaning.

steps.title: A second ברייתא clearly limits the exemption to the jaw
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא: if the כהן owns even 1/100 of the head, the butcher is exempt from the jaw but still owes all the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, it was taught: 'The head is mine and all the rest is yours.' Even if he owns only one hundredth of the head, he is exempt from the jaw and obligated in all the rest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, stronger challenge. This ברייתא says in plain words that only the jaw is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here there is no doubtful wording to explain away. The ברייתא says 'obligated in all the rest' outright. That directly goes against חייא בר רב's claim that one part exempts all three gifts.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And furthermore,' adding another argument
One hundredth, meaning even a tiny share
Obligated in all the rest of the gifts

phrases.english: And furthermore, it was taught:
'The head is mine and all the rest is yours':
phrases.notes: This is the כהן speaking to the butcher as they set up the partnership.

phrases.english: even if it is only one hundredth of the head,
he is exempt from the jaw but obligated in all the rest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, explicit source against חייא בר רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: חייא בר רב's ruling in step 15.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says outright that a share in the head exempts only the jaw and the rest are still owed.

steps.title: חייא בר רב is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that חייא בר רב's view is fully refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The refutation of חייא בר רב is a conclusive refutation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the argument. חייא בר רב's opinion cannot stand against these ברייתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the second ברייתא is clear, there is no way to defend חייא בר רב. The law follows רב הונא: a share in one part exempts only that part's gift.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation of an אמורא's view from a תנאי source

steps.whatToRemember: The halacha follows רב הונא. If a כהן or גוי shares in only one part (head, leg, or innards), the owner is exempt only from the gift of that part and still gives the others.

phrases.english: The refutation of Ḥiyya bar Rav is a conclusive refutation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge from step 20.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: חייא בר רב is refuted; partnership in one part exempts only the gift of that part, as רב הונא said.

steps.title: רב חסדא explains what misled חייא בר רב
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says a ברייתא misled חייא בר רב. It teaches that all 24 מתנות כהונה were given together with a כלל ופרט and a ברית מלח, and that keeping or breaking them is like keeping or breaking all of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: This ברייתא misled חייא בר רב, as it was taught: There are 24 gifts of כהונה, and all were given to אהרן and his sons with a כלל ופרט and a ברית מלח. Whoever keeps them is as if he kept the כלל ופרט and the ברית מלח, and whoever violates them is as if he violated the כלל ופרט and the ברית מלח.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that חייא בר רב is refuted, רב חסדא explains where his mistake came from. He quotes a ברייתא that counts and lists the 24 כהונה gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא counts the priestly gifts and arrives at exactly 24. Its list, given in the next steps, counts זרוע, לחיים and קבה together as a single gift. רב חסדא will explain in step 26 that this way of counting is what misled חייא בר רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Misled him, caused him to make a mistake
The gifts given to the כהנים; the ברייתא counts 24 of them
A general statement followed by a detailed list
A 'covenant of salt,' an unbreakable, everlasting covenant

steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא is not reopening the argument for חייא בר רב. The refutation still stands. He is only explaining which source led חייא בר רב to his wrong conclusion.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:

phrases.aramaic: הָא מַתְנִיתָא אַטְעִיתֵיהּ לְחִיָּיא בַּר רַב,
phrases.english: This ברייתא misled Ḥiyya bar Rav,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע מַתְּנוֹת כְּהוּנָּה הֵן,
phrases.english: as it was taught: There are twenty-four gifts of the priesthood,
and all of them were given to Aaron and his sons
with a general statement, a detailed list, and a covenant of salt.
phrases.notes: The general statement is במדבר 18:8, then the gifts are listed one by one, and the covenant of salt is במדבר 18:19.

phrases.english: Anyone who fulfills them

phrases.aramaic: כְּאִילּוּ קִיֵּים בִּכְלָל וּפְרָט וּבְרִית מֶלַח,
phrases.english: is as if he fulfilled the general statement, the detailed list, and the covenant of salt;
and anyone who violates them

phrases.aramaic: כְּאִילּוּ עוֹבֵר עַל בִּכְלָל וּפְרָט וּבְרִית מֶלַח.
phrases.english: is as if he violated the general statement, the detailed list, and the covenant of salt.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מַתְנִיתָא אַטְעִיתֵיהּ לְחִיָּיא בַּר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the refutation in step 21, explains the source behind חייא בר רב's mistaken view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חייא בר רב was misled by the ברייתא listing the 24 מתנות כהונה, which counts זרוע, לחיים and קבה as one gift.

steps.title: The three groups, and the ten gifts eaten in the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא divides the 24 gifts into three groups and lists the first group: ten gifts eaten only inside the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the 24 gifts: ten in the מקדש, four in ירושלים, and ten in the outlying areas. The ten in the מקדש are: the animal חטאת, the bird חטאת, the אשם ודאי, the אשם תלוי, the communal שלמים, the מצורע's log of oil, the שתי הלחם, the לחם הפנים, the leftovers of מנחות, and the מנחת העומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from Step 22 now spells out the 24 gifts. First it gives the three groups, then it names the ten gifts eaten only in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gifts are sorted by place. These first ten are קדשי קדשים, the holiest kind, so the כהנים may eat them only inside the עזרה. Every item here comes from a קרבן or a מנחה brought in the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: The gifts the Torah gives to the כהנים
The areas outside ירושלים, anywhere in ארץ ישראל
A guilt offering brought when a person is not sure he sinned
The measure of oil brought by a healed מצורע; the כהנים eat what is left of it
The showbread placed on the שולחן each שבת
The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן

phrases.english: And these are they: ten in the Temple,
phrases.notes: 'These' means the 24 gifts mentioned at the end of Step 22.

phrases.english: and four in Jerusalem, and ten in the outlying areas.
Ten in the Temple: an animal sin offering, and a bird sin offering,
a definite guilt offering, and a doubtful guilt offering,
and the communal peace offerings,
and the log of oil of a leper,
and the two loaves, and the showbread,
and the leftovers of meal offerings, and the omer meal offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא רב חסדא brought in Step 22, giving the actual list of 24 gifts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 24 gifts fall into three groups by place; ten are eaten only in the מקדש.

steps.title: The four gifts given in Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists the second group: four gifts the כהנים receive anywhere in ירושלים. The edible ones are eaten anywhere in the city, and the hides are given to them, not eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: The four in ירושלים are: the בכורה, the ביכורים, the portions taken from the תודה and the איל נזיר, and the hides of קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to the second group: four gifts that belong anywhere inside ירושלים, not only in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא groups the gifts by place: ten in the מקדש, four in ירושלים, and ten anywhere. These four are eaten and shared out anywhere in the city (Rashi). The בכורה, the ביכורים and the portions from the תודה and the איל נזיר are eaten there. The hides of the עולה, חטאת and אשם are not eaten; they are given to the כהנים as property. The portions from the תודה and from the איל נזיר are counted together as one gift, which is how the total comes out to four.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn kosher animal, given to the כהן
The first fruits brought to the מקדש
The portions 'lifted off' and given to the כהן
The ram a נזיר brings when he finishes his נזירות
The hides of sacrificial animals, given to the כהנים

phrases.english: And four in Jerusalem: the firstborn animal, and the first fruits,
and what is separated from the thanksgiving offering and from the nazir's ram,
phrases.notes: These two are counted as one gift, so the total stays at four.

phrases.english: and the hides of sacrificial animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same list, moving from the מקדש group to the ירושלים group.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four gifts belong anywhere in ירושלים: three are eaten in the city, and the hides are given to the כהנים.

steps.title: The ten gifts given anywhere in the land
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists the third group: ten gifts the כהן may have anywhere in ארץ ישראל, including the מתנות of זרוע, לחיים, and קבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ten in the outlying areas are: תרומה, תרומת מעשר, חלה, the first shearing, the gifts (foreleg, jaw, and maw), the redemption of the firstborn son, the redemption of the firstborn donkey, an ancestral field, a dedicated field, and the money for robbing a convert.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the list with the third group, ten gifts that are not tied to ירושלים at all. This completes the count of 24.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These gifts have no קדושת קרבן limiting where they are eaten, so the כהן may have them anywhere in the land. The line runs through seven items, and then the last line adds three more, שדה אחוזה, שדה חרמים, and גזל הגר, to make ten. The word מתנות here means the זרוע, לחיים, and קבה, the subject of our perek.

keyTerms.meaning: The tenth of his מעשר that the לוי gives to the כהן
The first shearing of the sheep's wool, given to the כהן
The lamb given to redeem a firstborn donkey
An inherited field dedicated to הקדש and not redeemed; it goes to the כהנים at the יובל
A field dedicated as חרם, which goes to the כהנים
Money owed for robbing a convert who died with no heirs; it is paid to the כהנים

steps.whatToRemember: The 24 gifts come in three groups: 10 in the מקדש, 4 in ירושלים, and 10 anywhere in the land. The מתנות of זרוע, לחיים, and קבה are in the last group.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the ברייתא רב חסדא said misled חייא בר רב. It counts זרוע, לחיים and קבה as a single item (מתנות), so he thought they form one unit, and that being exempt from one means being exempt from all three.

phrases.english: And ten in the outlying areas: תרומה, and תרומת מעשר,
and חלה, and the first shearing, and the gifts,
phrases.notes: 'The gifts' means the foreleg, jaw, and maw, the very gifts our perek is discussing.

phrases.english: and the redemption of the firstborn son, and the redemption of the firstborn donkey.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה, וּשְׂדֵה חֲרָמִים, וְגֶזֶל הַגֵּר.
phrases.english: And an ancestral field, and a dedicated field, and the robbery of a convert.
phrases.notes: These three are still part of this group. Add them to the seven above and you get ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא's list with the third and final group.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ten gifts, including the זרוע, לחיים, and קבה, may go to the כהן anywhere in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: What חייא בר רב thought
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains חייא בר רב's reasoning. Because the ברייתא counts the three animal gifts as one, he thought they really are one unit.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (חייא בר רב) thought: since the ברייתא counts these gifts as one, they must be one thing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא explains how the ברייתא misled חייא בר רב. He thought that counting זרוע, לחיים and קבה as one gift means they are truly one gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא's list of 24, the three gifts זרוע, לחיים and קבה take up only one place. חייא בר רב read this to mean they are one legal unit, so being exempt from one would make you exempt from all of them. This step only lays out his reasoning, and the next step will reject it.

keyTerms.meaning: counts, lists
as one
they are one (unit)

phrases.english: He thought:
phrases.notes: "He" is חייא בר רב, the one the ברייתא misled.

phrases.english: since the תנא counts the gifts as one,
phrases.notes: The gifts here are זרוע, לחיים and קבה from the list in step 25.

phrases.english: they must be one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא quoted in steps 22-25 misled חייא בר רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חייא בר רב thought that counting the three gifts as one means they are one legal unit.

steps.title: Counting as one does not make them one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects חייא בר רב's reading. The ברייתא also counts the מורם of a תודה and of an איל נזיר as one, yet nobody thinks they are one thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so! The ברייתא also counts the portion taken from a תודה and from an איל נזיר as one. Is that because they are one? Of course not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says חייא בר רב's reading is wrong. It proves this with a similar case in the same list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא also lists the כהן's portion from a תודה and from an איל נזיר as one gift. These clearly come from two different קרבנות. So being counted together in the list does not make two gifts one unit.

keyTerms.meaning: but it is not so
is that to say...? (a question that expects 'no')
the portion lifted off for the כהן
thanksgiving offering
the ram a נזיר brings when he finishes

phrases.english: But it is not so!
Is that to say that the portion lifted from a תודה and from an איל נזיר,
phrases.notes: These two also appear as one item in the ברייתא's list of 24 gifts.

phrases.english: which he counts as one,
is that because they are one?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reasoning given in step 26.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that being counted as one item in the list makes gifts one legal unit.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same list counts the תודה and איל נזיר portions as one, and they are clearly separate gifts.

steps.title: They are grouped because they are similar
steps.stepSummary: The real reason for counting them together is that they look alike. The same is true of זרוע, לחיים and קבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since they are like each other, he counts them as one. So too here, since they are like each other, he counts them as one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the true reason the ברייתא groups gifts together. It does so because they are similar, not because they are one unit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תודה and איל נזיר portions are grouped because they look alike. In the same way, זרוע, לחיים and קבה are grouped because they look alike. Each of these is still its own gift, so חייא בר רב's reading falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: they are similar to each other
so too, the same here

steps.whatToRemember: Being listed together in the ברייתא does not make gifts one unit. They are grouped only because they are alike, and each one stands on its own.

phrases.english: Rather, since they are similar to each other,
he counts them as one.
So too here: since they are similar to each other,
he counts them as one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct reading after the rejection in step 27.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא groups gifts that are similar. זרוע, לחיים and קבה remain separate gifts.

steps.title: Head to the ישראל, the rest to the כהן
steps.stepSummary: A new question: a כהן and a ישראל own an animal together, and the ישראל owns only the head. Do we follow the part that carries the gift, or the main part of the animal?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: if a כהן says 'the head is yours and all the rest is mine,' what is the law? Do we follow the obligation, which sits with the ישראל? Or do we follow the main part of the animal, which belongs to the כהן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. A ישראל owns only the head of an animal, which holds the לחיים gift, and a כהן owns everything else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to look at it. One way: the gift sits in the head, and the head belongs to the ישראל, so he must give it. The other way: the animal is mainly the כהן's, and a כהן's animal is exempt, so the ישראל is exempt too.

keyTerms.meaning: the obligation, meaning the part of the animal that holds the gift
the main part of the animal
we go after, we follow
or perhaps

phrases.english: A question was asked:
"The head is yours and all the rest is mine": what is the law?
phrases.notes: A כהן is saying this to a ישראל. The head is where the לחיים gift comes from.

phrases.english: Do we follow the obligation,
and the obligation is with the ישראל?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא בָּתַר עִיקַּר בְּהֵמָה אָזְלִינַן,
phrases.english: Or perhaps we follow the main part of the animal,
and the main part of the animal belongs to the כהן?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the חייא בר רב discussion has ended.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In a shared animal, does the gift obligation follow the owner of the gift part or the owner of most of the animal?

steps.title: A ברייתא about ראשית הגז
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא. A ישראל who shears sheep for a גוי or a כהן is exempt from ראשית הגז. So is someone who buys the shearing of a גוי's sheep.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if a גוי or a כהן gave their sheep to a ישראל to shear, he is exempt. One who buys the shearing of a גוי's sheep is exempt from ראשית הגז.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question. This first part sets up the proof, and the key line comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With wool, buying only the shearing of a גוי's sheep does not create a duty of ראשית הגז. Wool follows the owner of the sheep itself. This sets up a contrast with the animal gifts in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: the first shearing of wool, given to a כהן
to shear
exempt
one who buys the shearing (the wool still on the sheep)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A גוי or a כהן who handed over their sheep
to a ישראל to shear: he is exempt.
One who buys the shearing of a גוי's sheep
is exempt from ראשית הגז.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to settle the question asked in step 29.
steps.raayaObject: The question of whether we follow the obligation or the main part of the animal.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about ראשית הגז and the animal gifts.

steps.title: The animal gifts are stricter than wool
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that זרוע, לחיים and קבה are stricter than ראשית הגז. Someone who buys part of an animal from a כהן must give the gifts in the part he bought.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is a stringency in the זרוע, the לחיים and the קבה, more than in ראשית הגז.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the key line of the ברייתא. The animal gifts are stricter than wool when someone buys part of what belongs to a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With wool, the buyer is exempt. With the animal gifts, the buyer must give the gifts found in the part he bought, even if it is not the main part of the animal. That is exactly the case of a ישראל who owns only the head.

keyTerms.meaning: a stricter rule
more than

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. With wool, buying the shearing leaves you exempt. With the animal gifts, owning the part that holds the gift makes you obligated.

phrases.english: And this is a stricter rule
in the foreleg, the jaw and the maw
than in ראשית הגז.
phrases.notes: Here a buyer of part of an animal must still give the gifts in his part, unlike the buyer of wool.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 30 and gives the line that holds the proof.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the gift duty follows the owner of the gift part.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's line that the animal gifts are stricter than ראשית הגז.

steps.title: We follow the obligation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes from the ברייתא that we follow the part that carries the obligation. The ישראל who owns the head must give the לחיים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this that we follow the obligation. Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the question from step 29. We follow the part of the animal that holds the gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes a buyer of part of an animal give the gifts in his part. So the obligation goes with whoever owns that part, even if the main animal belongs to a כהן. The ישראל who owns the head must give the לחיים.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from it (a conclusion is proven)

steps.whatToRemember: In a shared animal, the gift duty follows the part that holds the gift (חיובא). It does not follow the owner of most of the animal.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule for partnerships with a כהן. The ישראל who owns the head, foreleg or maw must give the gifts in his part.

phrases.english: Learn from this that we follow the obligation.
Yes, learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא in steps 30-31.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We follow the obligation (בתר חיובא אזלינן). The ישראל who owns the head must give the לחיים.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: a sale 'except for the gifts'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. A כהן sold his animal to a ישראל but kept the gifts for himself. The ישראל is פטור from the מתנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the כהן said to the buyer, 'I am selling it to you except for the gifts,' the buyer is exempt from giving the gifts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a new line of the משנה to start a new discussion. This line sets up what the גמרא will talk about next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a ישראל who buys an animal from a כהן must give the מתנות, as we saw in the ברייתא earlier. Here the כהן kept the gifts out of the sale, so they still belong to the כהן. The ישראל never owned them, so he has nothing to give.

keyTerms.meaning: Except for the gifts. The כהן keeps the gifts out of the sale.
The gifts: the זרוע (foreleg), לחיים (jaw) and קבה (maw) given to a כהן.
Exempt; he does not have to do it.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the animal suddenly has no gifts. The gifts still exist. They simply stay with the כהן who sold the animal, so the buyer has nothing to give.

phrases.english: And if he said to him, "except for the gifts"
phrases.notes: The case is a כהן selling his animal to a ישראל. 'He' is the כהן, and 'him' is the buyer.

phrases.english: he is exempt from the gifts.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אָמַר לוֹ חוּץ מִן הַמַּתָּנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the question of shared ownership of an animal, the גמרא moves on to quote the next line of the משנה for a new discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a כהן sells an animal and keeps the gifts for himself, the ישראל buyer is exempt from the מתנות.
